text:
emily: Hi @people-ops — I just had a baby while traveling abroad and missed open enrollment. Can I add them retroactively?

people-ops: Congrats Emily :tada: You likely qualify for a QLE (birth). Since the birth occurred abroad we need the hospital birth record and passport/visa info once available. Don’t post PII here.

emily: Birth certificate is pending from local authorities. Hospital record has babys name and DOB. How long can retro coverage go back?

claire-hr: Carriers typically allow retro effective date to the date of birth if docs are provided within 30 days of the QLE. If documentation is delayed, some carriers still accept up to 60 days but its carrier-dependent. Payroll will be adjusted and any retro premiums may be pro-rated.

people-ops: Please upload scanned hospital record and any travel entry/exit stamps via Secure Upload -> Dependent Eligibility (International): https://redwood.hr/secure-upload. Benefits-bot will send a reminder.

benefits-bot: Upload reminder: submit docs within 30 days to avoid denial. Checklist: https://redwood.hr/dependents-checklist :lock:

emily: Uploaded hospital record and photos of passport page. Will send birth cert when available. Thanks!

people-ops: We received the upload. We'll submit to carrier and update you here. Expect 7-14 business days for confirmation. If carrier needs the official birth certificate later well request it.
